note: Single-pass extraction by Claude reading the paper text; evidence references sections/figures/tables. No multi-run validation.

components.description: Early/late fusion limitations motivate HELIOS's three-stage design and its empirical validation

nodes.name: Early fusion is query-independent
nodes.description: Early fusion builds retrieval units (fused blocks) independently of the query, often including query-irrelevant passages that distort similarity between fused blocks and queries.

nodes.name: Late fusion retrieves partial units
nodes.description: Late fusion retrieves single table segments or passages that may be only partially relevant, risking retrieval of a wrong table with overlapping terms (e.g. Grammy award tables).

nodes.name: Entity linking misses query-aware links
nodes.description: Early fusion relies on predefined entity-linking relationships that fail to capture query-dependent links needed to answer the query.

nodes.name: Semantic similarity can't do logical inference
nodes.description: Prior approaches rely on semantic similarity and so may fail to retrieve rows or passages requiring multi-hop or column-wise aggregation reasoning.

nodes.name: Bipartite graph formalization
nodes.description: Table segments and passages are formalized as two node sets of a bipartite graph; an early-fusion fused block is a star centered on a table-segment node and a late-fusion evidence chain is an edge.

nodes.name: Edge-based subgraph retrieval
nodes.description: HELIOS retrieves a bipartite subgraph by indexing offline-fused edges with ColBERTv2 multi-vector embeddings, using edges as a unit between star graphs and nodes to cut irrelevant context while avoiding partial information.

nodes.name: Query-relevant node expansion
nodes.description: HELIOS expands the candidate graph at node level with beam search (b=10) to find query-relevant edges missed by offline entity linking.

nodes.name: Star-based LLM refinement
nodes.description: HELIOS has an LLM reason over the expanded graph decomposed into smaller star graphs, enabling aggregation and multi-hop selection while reducing hallucination risk.

nodes.name: HELIOS leads OTT-QA retrieval
nodes.description: On OTT-QA dev, HELIOS beats COS by 19.0% average answer recall (42.6% at k=2), 39.9% nDCG@50 and 12.2% Hits@4K.

nodes.name: HELIOS leads end-to-end QA
nodes.description: On OTT-QA, HELIOS gets dev EM/F1 of 59.3/65.8 and test 57.0/64.3, above COS (56.9/63.2 dev, 54.9/61.5 test).

nodes.name: Edge unit is best granularity
nodes.description: Edge-based retrieval outperforms star-graph and node-based retrieval by 6.9% and 12.4% on average AR, and by 20% and 43.7% on nDCG@50.

nodes.name: QNE contributes
nodes.description: Removing query-relevant node expansion lowers AR by 2.1% on average, nDCG@50 by 4.2%, EM by 4.2% and F1 by 4.1%.

nodes.name: SLR helps at small k
nodes.description: Removing star-based LLM refinement drops AR@2 by 5.5% and nDCG@50 by 1.1%, with the effect mainly on small k and logical-inference queries.

nodes.name: Per-star prompts reduce hallucination
nodes.description: Prompting the LLM with individual star graphs instead of the full graph improves nDCG@50 by 12.4% (41.8 for the full-graph setting).

isolated_nodes.name: Competitive with HOLMES
isolated_nodes.description: In a distractor setting, HELIOS outperforms HOLMES by 88.4% EM and 58.1% F1, attributed to edge-level seed retrieval, question-conditioned LLM inference and preserving table structure.

isolated_nodes.name: Runtime trade-off
isolated_nodes.description: HELIOS runs 1.37x the time of COS for 39.9% higher nDCG@50; removing SLR gives 0.57x COS runtime with 38.4% nDCG@50 gain.

structural_reasoning: Argument runs from early/late fusion limitations through the graph formalization and three-stage HELIOS design to retrieval, QA, granularity and ablation results.
